# Visualizing the Triad: Schema, Signal, and Auto-Improvement as a Recursive Loop

The Triad is the architectural core of a self-improving system. Three nodes — Schema, Signal, and Auto-Improvement — form a closed loop where each concept is applied to itself recursively. This post visualises that structure and its relationship to recursion.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="The Triad: Schema, Signal, Auto-Improvement Recursive Loop" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:900px;height:auto;margin:1.5rem auto;">

## The Three Nodes

**Schema** defines structure. YAML configs, PostgreSQL table definitions, JSON validators, scoring weight files. Every system needs a schema before it can collect meaningful data. The recursive twist: the `intelligence_signals` table defines what signals ARE. The `scoring.yaml` file defines dimension weights. These are schemas about schemas.

**Signal** captures evidence. Menu present/select events. Prompt usage logs. Prediction hit/miss ratios. Without signals, you are just guessing. The recursive twist: the signal system signals about itself — menu events track their own effectiveness, prediction accuracy measures whether prediction is working.

**Auto-Improvement** closes the loop. Adaptive weights that learn from acceptance data. Scoring dimensions that reorder based on selection frequency. The recursive twist: the improver improves its own improvement criteria — accepted suggestions boost weight by 10%, rejected ones decay by 10%.

## Why Recursion Matters Here

A standard feedback loop improves the system. The Triad improves improvement itself. Each node applied to itself creates a compounding effect:

- `schema(schema)` — schemas that describe schemas
- `signal(signal)` — signals about signal effectiveness  
- `improve(improve)` — improvements to improvement criteria

This is not a metaphor. It is the actual implementation. The `improve.py` weights clamp between 0.3 and 3.0. After two accepts and one reject, "add_examples" went from 1.0 to 1.089. The system literally improves at improving.

## The Meta-Loop

At the bottom of the diagram sits a four-step cycle: **Observe, Measure, Adjust, Verify**. Every iteration of the Triad feeds into this cycle. Schema changes are verified against signal data. Signal collection is measured for coverage. Improvement adjustments are verified against outcome changes.

Every cycle compounds. Session 100 is smarter than session 1 — not because the code changed, but because the triad ran 100 times.

## The Numbers

After seeding realistic test data: 28 usage events across 18 sessions. Average shot score of 0.583. One co-affinity pair detected. The composite scoring surfaced a clear winner — the research synthesis prompt scored 0.729 vs the meta-prompt at 0.508.

Most systems are just storage. The Triad turns storage into intelligence through recursive self-application.
